tracks.narration: Two resistors stacked across a voltage source — what voltage shows up between them?
Send V in across R one and R two in series — Kirchhoff says the two drops have to add up to V in.
The same current flows through both, so V out equals V in times R two divided by R one plus R two.
Scrub R two. As it grows from small to large, V out climbs from near zero up toward V in — proportionally.
The output is V in scaled by R two's share of the total resistance — that's the voltage divider.
